text:
marta: FYI CI canary latency spike on the int8 packing perf test after today's merge. p95 jumped ~2.1x, blocking the rollout. ci-bot attached the failing job: rtx-serve-canary/pack-int8-perf-03

hao: looking into it. quick glance at the flamegraph shows a huge hot path in dequant_trampoline() — surprising for cached requests.

ryan: bisecting now across the last 6 merges. I can reproduce locally with the canary perf harness.

ci-bot: [CI] rtx-serve-canary perf test FAILED: p95_latency=210ms (baseline 95ms). Logs: https://ci.internal/redwood/builds/9876

jules: can you paste the small profile / hotspots?

hao: profile snippet pasted below:
```
hotspots:
- dequant_trampoline: 48%
- kernel_selector::select_best: 22%
- kv_cache_lookup: 8%
```
Seems dequant is consuming most cycles even when KV cache hits are common.

marta: Which models / sequence lengths are affected? Long-context only or short as well?

hao: Mostly short sequences (<=128). That points at the packing/kernel-selection policy — the new packing heuristic seems to prefer the compact quant path which pays a dequant penalty per token. For short sequences dequant overhead dominates.

tom: telemetry confirms — short-request distribution saw p50/p95 spikes, long-contexts unchanged.

ryan: bisect points to commit 0a3f2d8 which changed the kernel fallback ordering to favor compact/quant kernels.

jules: can we do a micro-fix in selector to prefer low-latency kernels for shorter seqs as a quick mitigation?

marta: QA needs a regression test to catch p95 regressions on short sequences. @anna-qa can you add a short-seq scenario to the perf suite?

anna-qa: on it — I'll add a perf job with seq_len distribution skewed to 32/64/128 and set an alert threshold for p95.

jules: proposed hotpatch (quick and dirty): in kernel_selector.cpp add an override:
```
// short sequence fast-path override
if (seq_len <= 256) return low_latency_kernel;
```
I'll open PR with benchmark before/after.

ryan: pushed revert PR to staging: PR#4567 (reverts 0a3f2d8). Deploying canary now.

sre-bot: deploy started to canary group 'int8-canary' (deploy id: d-2026-03-18-78).

ci-bot: canary perf run complete: p50=42ms (baseline 40ms), p95=98ms (baseline 95ms) — regression resolved in canary.

marta: :thumbsup: Revert merged to main. Blocker cleared. Follow-ups: replace dequant_trampoline with an optimized fused kernel and add selector unit tests to prevent recurrence.

tom: also add a microbench for the dequant path and wire up CPU-cycle counters to perf harness.

jules: created follow-up issue #1892 for optimized fused dequant kernel + perf tests and unit tests for kernel-selector heuristics.

ryan: note on quality: the selector change earlier favored quant kernels — that might have had minor quality differences. With revert in place we'll run evals to measure the delta and decide on safe thresholds.

hao: added an opt-in verbose flag to the runtime to log per-request kernel selection decisions (kernel id, seq_len, kv_hit) — will help debug if this crops up again.

marta: thanks all. leaving this thread open until QA perf job passes.
